principle: Choose age band, one primary learning objective and the teaching mechanism before writing narration or image prompts.

3-4.label: Preschool 3-4
3-4.narrationStyle: very short concrete sentences; repeat key words; one idea at a time
3-4.interactionStyle: name, point, repeat, choose between simple options
3-4.visualStyle: large simple subjects, very low clutter, strong shape and color contrast

5-8.label: Young learners 5-8
5-8.narrationStyle: short clear explanations with examples and causal language
5-8.visualStyle: clear explanatory scenes, simple diagrams, comparisons and real-world examples

9-12.label: Older kids 9-12
9-12.narrationStyle: clear explanatory language with cause-effect, comparisons and precise vocabulary
9-12.interactionStyle: predict, explain, compare, infer and apply
9-12.visualStyle: diagrams, maps, timelines, process visuals, comparisons and mini-documentary scenes

CONCEPT_STORY.label: Concept Story
CONCEPT_STORY.useWhen: An abstract idea becomes easier when it visibly causes events in a small story.

QUESTION_EXPLAINER.label: Question Explainer
QUESTION_EXPLAINER.useWhen: The topic starts with a why/how question and needs a clear explanation.

SONG_MEMORY.label: Song / Memory
SONG_MEMORY.useWhen: The main goal is memorizing a stable sequence, names, sounds or vocabulary.
SONG_MEMORY.note: Actual sung vocals are optional. A rhythmic spoken chant is allowed.

PRACTICE_REVEAL.label: Practice + Reveal
PRACTICE_REVEAL.useWhen: The child should actively answer several short questions.

VISUAL_COMPARE.label: Visual Compare
VISUAL_COMPARE.useWhen: Learning depends on seeing similarities, differences, categories or opposites.

MINI_DOCUMENTARY.label: Mini Documentary
MINI_DOCUMENTARY.useWhen: The topic is science, nature, geography, history, machines or a real-world system.

sceneFunctionRules.PROMISE: Tell the child what they will understand or be able to do.
sceneFunctionRules.SETUP: Introduce the objects/world needed for the concept.
sceneFunctionRules.QUESTION: State the central why/how question.
sceneFunctionRules.CONTEXT: Give only the background needed to understand the explanation.
sceneFunctionRules.DISCOVER: Let the concept visibly change or reveal something.
sceneFunctionRules.EXAMPLE: Show the taught idea in one concrete case.
sceneFunctionRules.REPEAT: Repeat the core item with variation for memory.
sceneFunctionRules.PRACTICE: Ask the child to predict, choose, count, match or answer.
sceneFunctionRules.PAUSE: Give thinking time without adding a new fact.
sceneFunctionRules.REVEAL: Show the correct answer and why it is correct.
sceneFunctionRules.APPLY: Use the idea in a new or real-world situation.
sceneFunctionRules.RECAP: Compress the core learning into memorable points.
sceneFunctionRules.CLOSING_QUESTION: End with a simple thought or observation prompt.

learningChannels.rule: Important ideas should normally be communicated through at least voice + visual. Add text only when it improves recognition or recall.

objectivePolicy.rule: Every scene must contribute to the primary objective or prepare/reinforce it.

characterPolicy.rule: A character is a teaching tool, not a branding requirement.
